title: Pic of an affine curve: quotient description, divisibility, finiteness
statement:
Let $C$ be a smooth affine connected curve over
algebraically closed $k$, and let $n$ be prime to
$\operatorname{char}k$. Let $\overline C$ be the
compactification ([lem-sc-compactification]) and
$S=\overline C\setminus C$ its (nonempty finite) complement; fix
$P_0\in S$. Then

$$
\operatorname{Pic}(C)\cong J_{\overline C}(k)/\Lambda,
\qquad
\Lambda:=\langle[P]-[P_0]:P\in S\rangle\subseteq J_{\overline C}(k),
$$

where $J_{\overline C}(k)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)$ is
the canonical identification of the
Jacobian of $\overline C$
([def-sc-jacobian], [thm-sc-jacobian-representability]), so $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ is a quotient
of the divisible group $J_{\overline C}(k)$ (there is
no degree map on $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ itself). In particular
$\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ is $n$-divisible and
$\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]$ is finite.

proof.text: Choose the smooth proper connected compactification with finite closed boundary using [lem-sc-compactification]. A smooth connected curve over an algebraically closed field is geometrically integral, so [thm-sc-jacobian-representability] supplies its Jacobian, the compatible degree-zero representation and its group isomorphism on rational points. The dimension clause agrees with the curve genus by [lem-pc-genus-agrees-sc]. Apply [lem-sc-pic-affine-quotient] to this data, obtaining a boundary point and the quotient isomorphism. Its generating set is finite: boundary closed points inject into the finite boundary, and each point determines at most one degree-zero Picard class and hence one Jacobian point. The subgroup closure of this finite set is finitely generated by AddSubgroup.fg_iff. This proves exists_addEquiv_pic_quotient.

The group $J_{\overline C}(k)$ is $n$-divisible by [thm-av-final](d), so its quotient $\operatorname{Pic}(C)=J_{\overline C}(k)/\Lambda$ is $n$-divisible. Apply [lem-sc-divisible-quotient-torsion] to $G=J_{\overline C}(k)$ and $\Lambda$. Its exact sequence identifies $\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]$ as an extension of $G[n]/\Lambda[n]$ by $\Lambda/n\Lambda$. Since $S$ is finite and $\Lambda$ is generated by the finitely many elements $[P]-[P_0]$, the latter quotient is finite. By [thm-av-final](c) (and [def-sc-mult-n]), $G[n]=J_{\overline C}[n](k)$ is finite. Hence $\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]$ is finite.
